source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading: This facility is attributed to STACK Infrastructure, whose own company site confirms active operations across a global footprint including 10 Americas locations (Atlanta, Calgary, Chicago, Dallas-Fort Worth, New Albany, Northern Virginia, Phoenix, Portland, Silicon Valley, and Toronto), 5 Asia Pacific locations, and 7 EMEA locations. Every state where this registry lists a Stack Infrastructure facility, Oregon (Portland market), California (Silicon Valley), Illinois (Chicago), and Virginia (Northern Virginia), matches a named company market. No founding date, headquarters, ownership structure such as a possible IPI Partners connection, or acquisition history, and no building specific address or individual MW figures for this particular registry row, were located in available sourcing this session.
profile.research_note: Market presence confirmed via operator own site; founding, ownership, and acquisition history not confirmed this session. Revisit with fresh WebSearch budget.

reading.body:
The operator's own specification page for STACK SVY02 publishes one figure: 560,440 square feet of technical space. Megawatts of IT load, power density targets, and cooling architecture are not published. Without a power figure, no translation into racks or accelerators is possible, and this site will not invent one. The square footage alone is large, roughly the footprint of ten city blocks under roof, but physical area is not a proxy for AI capacity without knowing how that space is loaded.

No certifications are listed in the published specifications, so this site cannot characterize what compliance regimes the campus meets or what regulated workloads it qualifies to host.

California is the largest state in this site's data set by both facility count and published megawatts, with 103 mapped facilities and 170 MW of published IT capacity across 5 of those sites. SVY02 does not appear among the five facilities that have published a megawatt figure, which is why it carries no rank by power in the state summary. The campus is mapped, it is large by floor area, and it sits in Santa Clara County at the center of the densest AI infrastructure cluster in the country, but without a published power number it cannot yet be weighed against its neighbors.
